issues.description: The problem statement and the reference solution define make_y_state to accept a depolarization parameter p (make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float)), but the template implementation's signature omits this parameter (def make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int)). This mismatch will prevent students from following the specification and from calling the function with the noise parameter as required by later tasks.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template function signature to match the specification and solution: def make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None. Update the template docstring to document the p parameter and ensure any calls in template helper code use the new signature.

issues.description: The function make_y_state is described in the problem statement and implemented in the solution with a depolarization parameter named 'p' (signature: make_y_state(circ, q, p: float)), but the template stub omits this parameter (signature: make_y_state(circ, q)). This parameter discrepancy makes it unclear to students which signature to implement and prevents directly following the problem instructions (preparing a noisy |Y> state with noise strength p).
issues.suggestedFix: Modify the template stub for make_y_state to include the depolarization parameter p with the same name and semantic meaning as in the problem statement and solution: def make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None. Update the template docstring to document the p parameter so students can implement the noisy |Y> preparation correctly.
